Chapter 9.04
FIREWORKS
Sections: 
9.04.010   Short title.
9.04.020   Declaration of policy.
9.04.030   Definitions.
9.04.040   Fireworks prohibited.
9.04.050   Permit for public display.
9.04.060   Financial requirements of applicant.
9.04.070   Permitted uses.
9.04.080   Conduct of display.
9.04.090   Seizure.
9.04.100   Violation—Penalty.
9.04.010   Short title.
   This chapter may be cited and shall be known as the Pima County fireworks
ordinance.
(Prior code § 41.20.010)
9.04.020   Declaration of policy.
   The purpose of this chapter is to protect the general public from the
hazardous use, sale and display of fireworks and to require competent operators
in the display of fireworks.
(Prior code § 41.20.020)
9.04.030   Definitions.
   A.   "Fireworks" shall be defined as in A.R.S. Section 36-1601(1).
   B.   "Governing body" means the board of supervisors of Pima County as to
the area within the county but without the corporate limits of an incorporated
city or town.
   C.   "Person" includes individual, partnership, firm, corporation or
association.
   D.   "Pyrotechnic operator" means a person, of good character, who has shown
to the board of supervisors and/or the sheriff that they have the ability and
knowledge through experience or training to safely and properly handle
fireworks.
(Prior code § 41.20.030)
9.04.040   Fireworks prohibited.
   A.   Except as otherwise provided by this section, it is unlawful to sell,
offer, or expose for sale; use; explode or possess any fireworks.
   B.   This chapter shall not be construed to prohibit or restrict the
manufacture or possession, by a qualified pyrotechnic operator, of aerial set
pieces designed for use in pyrotechnical displays, or the display of such set
pieces in accordance with the terms of this chapter.
(Prior code § 41.20.040)
9.04.050   Permit for public display.
   A.   Application for a permit shall be made in writing not less than 45 days
prior to the date of the display. Each applicant must notify any neighbors
within 1,000 feet of the site by any effective means of notification including,
but not limited to, direct mail, door flyers, signs or communication through
homeowners or neighborhood associations. The means of notice shall be specified
on the application for a permit. Every display shall be handled by a
pyrotechnic operator, and shall be of a character and located, discharged and
fired so that it will not be hazardous to property or endanger any person.
Before a permit is granted, the operator, location and handling of the display
shall be approved by the board of supervisors after investigation and approval
by the sheriff. After a permit is granted, the sale, possession, use and
distribution of fireworks for the display shall be lawful for that purpose
only. No permit is transferable or assignable and will be void if transferred
or assigned.
   B.   Public displays of fireworks may only be set off:
      1.   Between sunset December 31 to 1:00 a.m. January 1; and
      2.   Between sunset and 10:00 p.m. on all other days in which public
displays of fireworks are allowed.
(Prior code § 41.20.050) (Ord. 2025-11 §§ 1 - 3, 2025)
9.04.060   Financial requirements of applicant.
   A.   The board of supervisors shall require each applicant to give a
satisfactory bond in a principal amount not less than five hundred dollars,
conditioned upon payment of all damages which may be caused to persons or
property by reason of the display.
   B.   Each applicant shall be required to hold harmless the county for any
and all damages or injury occurring as a result of the possession, use or
display of fireworks, and each permittee shall defend all actions brought
against the county with relation to the permit for fireworks, and shall pay all
judgments against the county in relation to the permit and shall appeal at the
option of the county all judgments against the county resulting from the
granting of the permit.
   C.   Each applicant shall include with the application a copy of the
certificate of liability insurance for a minimum of ten million dollars with
Pima County listed as additional insured.
(Prior code § 41.20.060) (Ord. 2025-11 § 4, 2025)
9.04.070   Permitted uses.
   This chapter shall not be construed to prohibit:
   A.   The sale at wholesale by a resident wholesaler, dealer or jobber of
fireworks which are not prohibited by this chapter;
   B.   The sale of fireworks which are to be and are shipped directly out of
the state;
   C.   The use of fireworks by railroads or other transportation agencies for
signal purposes or illumination;
   D.   The use of fireworks or explosives, or both, by farmers, ranchers and
their employees, and by state and federal employees who manage wildlife
resources, to rally, drive or otherwise disperse concentrations of wildlife for
the purpose of protecting property or wildlife;
   E.   No fireworks display shall occur for longer than thirty minutes.
   F.    No fireworks display shall be held if the wind reaches a velocity of
more than ten miles per hour at the scheduled display time or at any time
during the display, verified by the appropriate fire department/district.
   G.   No public fireworks displays shall be held if the USDA Forest Service
fire restriction is at a stage three.
   H.   A firework display that occurs during a USDA Forest Service fire
restriction stage one or stage two fire restriction shall require a minimum of
one dedicated brush truck with sufficient staffing to operate said vehicle at
the site of the display both prior to and throughout the event. The total
number of equipment and staffing shall be approved by the chief of the
appropriate fire department/district. Firework displays are prohibited during
designated periods of extreme fire danger or red flag warning conditions.
   I.   All fireworks, articles and items at places of display shall be stored
in a manner and in a place secure from fire, accidental discharge, and theft or
other potential hazards, and in a manner approved by the governmental agency
having jurisdiction.
   J.   The applicant must:
      1.   Notify the appropriate fire department/district and schedule on-site
standby fire suppression equipment as necessary for the site as determined by
the appropriate fire chief during the display.
      2.   Clear a firing area and a drop area for spent fireworks as
designated by the local fire department/district.
      3.   Cancel any display scheduled if the wind speed within ten feet of
ground level, is higher than ten miles per hour at the scheduled display time
or at any time during the display, verified by the appropriate fire department/
district.
      4.   Remedy any fire or property damage including native ground cover and
tree and shrub replacement based on what existed previously including planting
and irrigation as appropriate.
(Prior code § 41.20.080) (Ord. 2025-11 §§ 5, 6, 2025)
9.04.080   Conduct of display.
   A.   No permit shall be granted for any display of fireworks where the
discharge, failure to fire, faulty firing, or fallout of any fireworks or other
objects would endanger persons, buildings, structures, forests, or brush, nor
in any case where the point at which the fireworks are to be fired is less than
two hundred feet from the nearest permanent building, public highway, railroad,
or other means of travel, or fifty feet from the nearest above ground telephone
or telegraph line, tree or other overhead obstruction, or one hundred feet from
a high-tension wire. In no case shall a display be fired within five hundred
feet of a school, theater, church, hospital, or similar institution without
written approval by the institution and special approval by the board of
supervisors.
   B.   Spectators at a display of fireworks shall be restrained behind lines
or barriers as designated by local authorities but in no case less than two
hundred feet from the point at which the fireworks are to be discharged. Only
authorized persons and those in actual charge of the display shall be allowed
inside these lines or barriers during the unloading, preparation, firing and
clean-up period of fireworks.
   C.   All fireworks that fire a projectile shall be so set up that the
projectile will go into the air as nearly as possible in a vertical direction.
   D.   Any fireworks that remain unfired after the display is concluded shall
be immediately disposed of or removed in a manner safe for the particular type
of fireworks. The debris from the discharged fireworks shall be properly
disposed of by the operator before he leaves the premises. The operator, upon
conclusion of the display, shall make a complete and thorough search for any
unfired fireworks or pieces which have failed to fire or function and shall
dispose of them in a safe manner. Such search shall be instituted at the
earliest possible time following the conclusion of the display but in no event
later than the first period of daylight which follows.
   E.   No fireworks display shall be held during any storm or wind in which
the wind reaches a velocity of more than ten miles per hour.
   F.   All fireworks, articles and items at places of display shall be stored
in a manner and in a place secure from fire, accidental discharge, and theft or
other potential hazards, and in a manner approved by the governmental agency
having jurisdiction.
(Prior code § 41.20.080)
9.04.090   Seizure.
   The Arizona Highway Patrol or any sheriff or other peace officer shall
seize, remove, or cause to be removed, at the expense of the owner, all
fireworks or combustibles offered or exposed for sale, stored or possessed in
violation of this chapter.
(Prior code § 41.20.090)
9.04.100   Violation—Penalty.
   A person violating a provision of this chapter is guilty of a class three
misdemeanor.
(Prior code § 41.20.100)
Chapter 9.08
EMERGENCY VEHICLE PERMITS
Sections: 
9.08.010   Purpose.
9.08.020   Definitions.
9.08.030   Emergency equipment standards.
9.08.040   Emergency management director.
9.08.050   Emergency vehicle permit required.
9.08.060   Application for emergency vehicle permit.
9.08.070   Issuance of emergency vehicle permit.
9.08.080   Displaying of emergency vehicle permit.
9.08.090   Expiration and renewal of emergency vehicle permit.
9.08.100   Transfer or replacement of emergency vehicle permit.
9.08.110   Responsibility of emergency vehicle permit holders.
9.08.120   Denial, suspension or revocation of emergency vehicle permit.
9.08.130   Right of appeal.
9.08.010   Purpose.
   The purpose of this chapter is to regulate the issuance of emergency vehicle
permits pursuant to Title 28, Sections 101 and 624, Arizona Revised Statutes.
(Ord. 1996-5 (part), 1996)
9.08.020   Definitions.
   The following definitions, in addition to those in Section
10.04.020, shall apply in the interpretation and enforcement of this chapter:
   A.   "Authorized emergency vehicle" means:
      1.   Vehicles of a fire department;
      2.   Vehicles of a police department;
      3.   Ambulance and emergency vehicles of municipal departments and public
service corporations designated or authorized by the Department or local
authorities, or other ambulances, fire trucks and rescue vehicles authorized at
the sole discretion of the Department and that meet liability insurance
requirements prescribed by the Department.
   B.   "Department" is the Arizona Department of Transportation.
   C.   "Director" is the director of the Tucson/Pima County office of
emergency management as designated by the county administrator and city
manager.
   D.   "Permit" refers to emergency vehicle permits.
(Ord. 1996-5 (part), 1996)
9.08.030   Emergency equipment standards.
   A.   The vehicle for which the emergency vehicle permit is issued shall at
all times when in use as such be equipped with at least one of the following: a
red or red and blue lighted lamp; a red or red and blue lighted lens visible
under normal conditions from a distance of five hundred feet to the front of
the vehicle. The vehicle must also be equipped with, and while in motion must,
as reasonably necessary, activate a bell, siren or exhaust whistle.
   B.   The vehicle for which the emergency vehicle permit is issued is subject
to inspection by the director upon notice duly given.
(Ord. 1996-5 (part), 1996)
9.08.040   Emergency management director.
   The director may make rules and regulations concerning the issuance of
emergency vehicle permits.
(Ord. 1996-5 (part), 1996)
9.08.050   Emergency vehicle permit required.
   No person, with the exception of any federal, state, county, city or town
vehicles, shall operate an emergency vehicle without first obtaining an
authorized emergency vehicle permit.
(Ord. 1996-5 (part), 1996)
9.08.060   Application for emergency vehicle permit.
   A.   An application for an emergency vehicle permit shall be made to the
director.
   B.   The application for an emergency vehicle permit shall be made upon a
form furnished by the director. It shall contain such information concerning
the applicant's background and experience as the director prescribes, in
addition to other information required by law.
(Ord. 1996-5 (part), 1996)
9.08.070   Issuance of emergency vehicle permit.
   The director may issue emergency vehicle permits only for authorized
emergency vehicles.
(Ord. 1996-5 (part), 1996)
9.08.080   Displaying of emergency vehicle permit.
   The emergency vehicle permit identification sticker must be displayed on the
rear bumper of the vehicle at all times. The emergency vehicle permit
certificate shall be carried in the vehicle at all times.
(Ord. 1996-5 (part), 1996)
9.08.090   Expiration and renewal of emergency vehicle permit.
   All emergency vehicle permits issued shall expire on December 31st of the
year issued. Emergency vehicle permit renewal is by application annually by
form and manner determined by the director.
(Ord. 1996-5 (part), 1996)
9.08.100   Transfer or replacement of emergency vehicle permit.
   A.   Emergency vehicle permits shall not be transferable to any other
person, company or vehicle.
   B.   In the event of a name change, not involving a change of an address of
the permittee, the emergency vehicle permit shall be returned to the director
for cancellation and a new emergency vehicle permit application form shall be
submitted. A new emergency vehicle permit for the unexpired term will be
issued.
   C.   In the event the vehicle for which the emergency vehicle permit is
issued is disposed of, the emergency vehicle permit shall be removed from the
vehicle and the emergency vehicle permit returned to the director for
cancellation.
   D.   In the event of loss, destruction or mutilation of the emergency
vehicle permit, the permittee to whom it was issued may obtain a duplicate upon
application to the director.
(Ord. 1996-5 (part), 1996)
9.08.110   Responsibility of emergency vehicle permit holders.
   A.   The person, persons or corporation to which an emergency vehicle permit
is issued shall be responsible for the actions of the driver of the permitted
vehicle when operated under emergency conditions.
   B.   Should a provision of the Arizona Revised Statutes or the terms under
which the emergency vehicle permit was issued be violated, the emergency
vehicle permit will be subject to suspension or revocation by the director upon
notice given.
(Ord. 1996-5 (part), 1996)
9.08.120   Denial, suspension or revocation of emergency vehicle permit.
   An emergency vehicle permit may be denied, suspended or revoked by the
director for failure to comply with any provision of this chapter, any
provision of the Arizona Revised Statutes, or regulations promulgated pursuant
to this chapter upon due notice being given.
(Ord. 1996-5 (part), 1996)
9.08.130   Right of appeal.
   If in the opinion of the applicant or permittee the act of denial,
suspension or revocation of an emergency vehicle permit by the director was
unjust, arbitrary or capricious, he may request in writing within sixty days of
denial, suspension or revocation a public hearing before the Pima County board
of supervisors.
(Ord. 1996-5 (part), 1996)
Chapter 9.12
OFF-ROAD RECREATIONAL MOTOR VEHICLES
Sections: 
9.12.010   Definitions.
9.12.020   Prohibited vehicle uses.
9.12.030   Identification and proof of vehicle ownership.
9.12.040   Exempt vehicle uses.
9.12.050   Exempt locations.
9.12.060   Government property.
9.12.070   Civil penalties.
9.12.010   Definitions.
   For the purposes of this chapter:
   A.   "Off-road recreational motor vehicle" or "vehicle" means three and four
wheel vehicles manufactured for recreational nonhighway all terrain travel.
   B.   "Operate" means driving or having actual physical control over the
vehicle.
   C.   "Wash" or "riverbed" means a watercourse having beds, banks, sides and
channels through which either waters currently flow or through which
floodwaters flow periodically.
(Reso. 1988-43 § 1, 1988; Ord. 1987-209 § 1 (part), 1987)
9.12.020   Prohibited vehicle uses.
   No person shall operate an off-road recreational motor vehicle:
      1.   Upon any portion of any publicly owned washes or riverbeds within
the county except to cross such washes or riverbeds from one bank to another
within the boundaries of an existing, clearly defined highway, street, road,
primitive roadway, trail or traveled way; or
      2.   Upon privately owned lands without notarized written consent of the
owner, the owner's agent or the person in lawful possession of such property.
Such written consent shall be kept within a person's possession while operating
a vehicle and shown upon the request of a peace officer; or
      3.   In such a way as to knowingly cause or contribute to visible dust
emissions which then cross property lines into a residential, recreational,
institutional, educational, retail, sales, hotel or business premises; or
      4.   At a speed greater than is reasonable and prudent under the
circumstances, conditions and actual and potential hazards then existing. In
every event, speed shall be so controlled as may be necessary to avoid
colliding with any object, person, animal life or other vehicle so as to comply
with the duty of all persons to exercise reasonable care for the protection of
others.
(Reso. 1988-43 § 1, 1988; Ord. 1987-209 § 1 (part), 1987)
9.12.030   Identification and proof of vehicle ownership.
   A.   All operators of off-road recreational vehicles shall carry proof of
vehicle ownership, or a rental agreement, and a driver's license while
operating such vehicles and shall show such documents upon the request of a
peace officer. If an operator is unlicensed then recent picture identification
shall be carried.
   B.   For the purpose of this section, identification for minors may include
a school picture identification with school or home address or a notarized
statement consisting of a minor's physical description and home address which
is signed by a parent or guardian.
(Reso. 1988-43 § 1, 1988; Ord. 1987-209 § 1 (part), 1987)
9.12.040   Exempt vehicle uses.
   The provisions of this chapter shall not apply to a vehicle being used for:
      1.   Ranching or agricultural purposes;
      2.   Grading, construction or building trade purposes;
      3.   Mining purposes;
      4.   Licensed off-road business operations such as land surveying, public
utility companies, sand and gravel operations and other similar enterprises;
      5.   Authorized emergency vehicle including towing services;
      6.   Governmental purposes by a government employee;
      7.   Golf carts and golf courses.
(Reso. 1988-43 § 1, 1988; Ord. 1987-209 § 1 (part), 1987)
9.12.050   Exempt locations.
   The provisions of this chapter shall not apply:
   A.   To vehicle operators on their own property, except when creating dust
emissions as set forth in subsection (3) of Section
9.12.020;
   B.   On any dedicated public highway, street, road or alley or parking lot
generally open to the public for the purpose of vehicular travel;
   C.   Within the limits of any incorporated city or town.
(Reso. 1988-43 § 1, 1988; Ord. 1987-209 § 1 (part), 1987)
9.12.060   Government property.
   Nothing in this chapter shall be deemed to interfere with the right of any
government agency to regulate, prohibit or permit the use of off-road
recreational vehicles on property owned by it or under its control and
jurisdiction, nor to permit or authorize any trespass or nuisance.
(Reso. 1988-43 § 1, 1988; Ord. 1987-209 § 1 (part), 1987)
9.12.070   Civil penalties.
   Violation of this chapter shall constitute a civil offense and shall be
punishable by a fine, fixed by the court, of not less than fifty dollars nor
more than seven hundred fifty dollars. In the case of actual damage to person
or property or a third offense within a twelve-month period, the court shall
assess a fine of not less than two hundred fifty dollars nor more than seven
hundred fifty dollars. The imposition of a fine under this section shall not be
suspended.
(Reso. 1988-43 § 1, 1988; Ord. 1987-209 § 1 (part), 1987)
Chapter 9.13
ALARMS*
Sections: 
9.13.010   Purpose and intent.
9.13.020   Findings.
9.13.030   Definitions.
9.13.040   Excessive false alarms prohibited.
9.13.050   False robbery alarms prohibited.
9.13.060   Penalties.
9.13.070   Common cause exception.
9.13.080   Alarm operator.
9.13.090   Alarm company duties.
9.13.100   Penalties.
9.13.110   Corrective measures.
9.13.120   Recent installations.
9.13.130   Exemptions.
9.13.140   Evidence.
9.13.010   Purpose and intent.
   This section is intended to encourage the improvement in reliability of
alarm systems and devices and ensure that sheriff's personnel will not be
diverted from responding to actual criminal activity as a result of responding
to false alarms. The regulation is malum prohibitum ; no knowledge or lack of
due care is required to prove a violation.
(Ord. 1994-36 § 1 (part), 1994)
9.13.020   Findings.
   False alarms and false robbery alarms constitute a substantial public danger
and a substantial public expense. Of alarm notice received by the Pima County
sheriff's department, experience has shown that overwhelming majority are
false. Law enforcement resources are diverted from other duties by these
alarms. Law enforcement personnel and the public are endangered by the need for
urgent response to these alarms.
(Ord. 1994-36 § 1 (part), 1994)
9.13.030   Definitions.
   The following words and phrases, whenever used in this chapter, shall be
construed as defined in this section, unless the context requires otherwise:
   A.   "Act of nature" means unusual, extraordinary, sudden and unexpected
manifestation of the forces of nature, the effects of which cannot be prevented
by reasonable human care, skill or foresight.
   B.   "Alarm system" means any mechanical or electrical device which is used
to help protect persons, building or premises in emergencies through the
emission of a sound or the transmission of a signal or message.
   C.   "False alarm" means an alarm signal or message, other than a robbery
alarm, indicating an emergency and causing a deputy to respond which is not
caused by or the result of an actual emergency entry, or an act of nature.
   D.   "False robbery alarm" means a message or signal which indicates a
robbery, causing a deputy to respond, which is not caused by or the result of
an actual or attempted robbery or act of nature.
   E.   "Person" means any natural person, employee, firm, partnership,
association or corporation.
   F.   "Common cause" means a technical difficulty or malfunction which causes
an alarm system to generate a series of false alarms.
   G.   "Emergency" means the commission or attempted commission of an offense
in violation of A.R.S. Title 13 or a medical emergency.
(Ord. 1994-36 § 1 (part), 1994)
9.13.040   Excessive false alarms prohibited.
   It shall be unlawful and constitute a civil violation for any person to own,
purchase, lease, contract for or otherwise obtain, or operate an alarm system
which had five or more false alarms within any consecutive three-hundred-sixty-
five-day period. Each false alarm generated in excess of five within any
consecutive three-hundred-sixty-five-day period is a separate violation of this
section.
(Ord. 1994-36 § 1 (part), 1994)
9.13.050   False robbery alarms prohibited.
   It shall be unlawful and constitute a civil violation for any person to own,
purchase, lease, contract for or otherwise to operate an alarm system which
generated five or more false robbery alarms within any consecutive three-
hundred-sixty-five-day period. Each false alarm generated in excess of five
within any consecutive three-hundred-sixty-five-day period is a separate
violation of this section.
(Ord. 1994-36 § 1 (part), 1994)
9.13.060   Penalties.
   A.   A person found responsible for a fifth false alarm in violation of
Section
9.13.040 shall be punished by a minimum civil penalty of one hundred twenty-
five dollars; a penalty not to exceed one thousand dollars may be imposed.
False alarm incidents may form the basis of more than one violation of Section
9.13.040.
   B.   A person found responsible for a sixth false alarm in violation of
Section
9.13.040 shall be punished by a minimum civil penalty of two hundred fifty
dollars; a penalty not to exceed one thousand dollars may be imposed. False
alarm incidents may form the basis of more than one violation of Section
9.13.040.
   C.   A person found responsible for a seventh false alarm in violation of
Section
9.13.040 shall be punished by a minimum civil penalty of three hundred seventy-
five dollars; a penalty not to exceed one thousand dollars may be imposed.
False alarm incidents may form the basis of more than one violation of Section
9.13.040.
   D.   The fine amount for a person found responsible for each false alarm
occurring thereafter within the same three-hundred-sixty-five-day period shall
increase by increments of not less that one hundred twenty-five dollars nor
more than one thousand dollars for each violation.
   E.   A person found responsible for a violation of Section
9.13.050 shall be punished by a minimum civil penalty of five hundred dollars;
a penalty not to exceed one thousand dollars may be imposed.
   F.   No penalty imposed under this chapter may be suspended, waived or
otherwise made conditional in sanctioning a person found responsible of
violations of the offenses set out in this chapter.
   G.   A report from the Pima County sheriff's department documenting a
sheriff's response to an alarm and an investigation which revealed no emergency
shall constitute prima facie evidence of a false alarm.
(Ord. 1994-36 § 1 (part), 1994)
9.13.070   Common cause exception.
   False alarms generated by a common cause shall be counted as one false alarm
if, and only if, the false alarms occurred within a seventy-two-hour period and
corrective action is taken and immediate notice of such action is provided to
the sheriff's department, and during the next thirty-day period there are no
false alarms generated by that documented cause.
(Ord. 1994-36 § 1 (part), 1994)
9.13.080   Alarm operator.
   A.   The operator of any alarm system, whether at a business or residence,
shall be responsible for instructing all persons who are authorized to place
the device or system into operation in the appropriate method of operation,
advising them of the provisions of this chapter, and emphasizing the importance
of avoiding false alarms.
   B.   The operator of any alarm system, whether at a business or residence,
shall conspicuously place on the premises a notice identifying the alarm
company or service to whom the premises subscribes and who is available to
respond to an alarm activation, or a notice provided by the sheriff's
department designed to allow notification of the operator or an authorized
representative available to respond to an alarm activation, or other such
notice which shall include the name, address and telephone number of the
primary person and at least one alternate available to respond to an alarm
activation.
(Ord. 1994-36 § 1 (part), 1994)
9.13.090   Alarm company duties.
   A.   When the sheriff's department is notified of an alarm activation by an
alarm company, service or operator, the notifying party shall advise the
sheriff's department if an authorized representative will respond to the alarm
and, if so, if the representative will arrive within thirty minutes at the
location of the alarm. If the department is advised there will be a response
within thirty minutes, it shall constitute a civil infraction to fail to
respond within the thirty-minute period.
   B.   If an alarm signal is received at a central station, the alarm company
or service operating the central station shall, when it advises the sheriff's
department of the alarm, also immediately notify the operator of the alarm
system of the alarm.
   C.   An alarm company or service shall inform purchasers of alarm systems or
services of the provision of this chapter. This provision shall not apply to
alarm systems which generate only an audible alarm at the location of the
alarm.
   D.   The alarm company or service shall maintain a record of alarm
activation notification for a one-year period following notification. Records
shall include the name and phone number of the person notified of the alarm
activation, and the time notification was given.
   E.   It shall constitute a civil infraction for an alarm company, service,
or operator to fail to comply with any of the provisions of Sections
9.13.080 and
9.13.090.
(Ord. 1994-36 § 1 (part), 1994)
9.13.100   Penalties.
   Unless otherwise provided in this chapter, when a violation of Sections
9.13.080 and
9.13.090 is determined, the following penalties shall be imposed:
   A fine of not less than fifty dollars nor more than one thousand dollars per
violation. The imposition of a fine under this chapter shall not be suspended.
(Ord. 1994-36 § 1 (part), 1994)
9.13.110   Corrective measures.
   It shall be a defense to any incident prohibited in this chapter that a
deputy did not actually respond to an alarm as a result of notice to the Pima
County sheriff's department from the owner, lessee, purchaser or operator of
the alarm system that the alarm was false.
(Ord. 1994-36 § 1 (part), 1994)
9.13.120   Recent installations.
   New installed and reinstalled alarm systems shall not be subject to the
provision of these section relating to the county assessment of false alarms
for a period of thirty days from the date the alarm system becomes operational
if the alarm owner notifies the Pima County sheriff's department in writing
within ten days of the completion of the installation or reinstallation. The
written notice shall specify the date the system was installed or reinstalled;
and if reinstalled, the notice shall also describe the nature and extent of the
reinstallation.
(Ord. 1994-36 § 1 (part), 1994)
9.13.130   Exemptions.
   The provisions of this chapter shall not be applicable to audible alarms
affixed to automobiles or to alarm systems operated by governmental units.
(Ord. 1994-36 § 1 (part), 1994)
9.13.140   Evidence.
   In any court action to enforce this chapter, official law enforcement
records shall be received in evidence without other foundation.
(Ord. 1994-36 § 1 (part), 1994)
Chapter 9.16
TUCSON-PIMA COUNTY EMERGENCY SERVICES COMMISSION
Sections: 
9.16.010   Created—Membership.
9.16.020   Terms of office.
9.16.030   Vacancies.
9.16.040   Members to serve without compensation.
9.16.050   Duties, powers, and functions.
9.16.060   Chairperson.
9.16.070   Emergency services agency—Director of emergency services generally.
9.16.080   Method of commission operation.
9.16.090   Definition, responsibilities and duties of the director of emergency
services.
9.16.100   Future participation in Tucson-Pima County emergency services plan.
9.16.010   Created—Membership.
   There is created a joint municipal and county agency, to be called "The
Tucson-Pima County Emergency Service Commission." The voting members of the
commission consist of ten persons originally selected in the following manner:
the chairperson of the Pima County board of supervisors submits a list of ten
names and the mayor submits a list of ten names. Ten persons are selected from
among the twenty names submitted. Each of the supervisors of Pima County has
one and four-tenths votes; however, the total number of supervisor votes
remains at seven in the event the number of supervisors is changed. The mayor
has one vote. However, the total number of votes for the mayor and council
remains at seven votes in the event the number of councilmen is changed.
(Reso. 1990-135 § 1, 1990; Ord. 1985-142 § 1 (part), 1985)
9.16.020   Terms of office.
   The terms of office of the members of the Tucson-Pima County emergency
services commission are as follows: four members are appointed for a term of
one year commencing as of the date of the original Ordinance No. 1963-21 passed
by the Pima County board of supervisors and the passage of a corresponding
ordinance by the mayor and council, whichever is the later date; three members
are appointed for a term of two years commencing on such date; three members
are appointed for a term of three years from the expiration of the original
term of office.
(Reso. 1990-135 § 1, 1990; Ord. 1985-142 § 1 (part), 1985)
9.16.030   Vacancies.
   Whenever there are vacancies, the Tucson-Pima County emergency services
commission, by absolute majority vote, shall submit one name for each vacancy
to be filled to the Pima County board of supervisors, the mayor and council of
the city of Tucson, and the appropriate governmental body of any future
participating political subdivisions. In order that the nominee be appointed, a
majority vote of each of the above governing bodies will be required. All such
appointments made subsequent to the original appointment will be for a term of
four years.
(Ord. 1991-45 § 1, 1991: Reso. 1990-135 § 1, 1990; Ord. 1985-142 § 1 (part),
1985)
9.16.040   Members to serve without compensation.
   Voting members of the commission serve without compensation, but may be
reimbursed for traveling and other necessary expenses incurred in the
performance of their duties as provided for public officers.
(Reso. 1990-135 § 1, 1990; Ord. 1985-142 § 1 (part), 1985)
9.16.050   Duties, powers, and functions.
   A.   The commission shall advise the director of emergency services on the
following:
      1.   The development of disaster control and post-disaster recovery;
      2.   The development of emergency services policies and recommendations
for implementation of these plans insofar as city, county, state and federal
means are available.
   B.   The commission is considered an advisory and planning body only. It has
no operational functions other than those which may, from time to time, be
delegated to it by ordinance or other means.
(Reso. 1990-135 § 1, 1990; Ord. 1985-142 § 1 (part), 1985)
9.16.060   Chairperson.
   There is a chairperson of the commission who is chosen by an absolute
majority vote of the voting members of the commission. The chairperson shall
serve for a one (1) year term. The term shall start at midnight on the date of
his appointment. The chairperson may be elected for additional terms.
(Reso. 1990-135 § 1, 1990; Ord. 1985-142 § 1 (part), 1985)
9.16.070   Emergency services agency—Director of emergency services generally.
   The director of the Tucson-Pima County emergency services agency will select
and appoint a manager to assist the director in carrying out the
responsibilities and duties of the director of emergency services. The manager
of emergency services will be selected and appointed by the director through
Pima County merit system procedures. The director, or the manager of emergency
services when instructed by the director, also is the eleventh member and vice-
chairperson of the commission, in order to insure continuity of purpose and
direction between the agency and the commission. The director, however, has no
vote. The director shall assume the chairperson's position in case the
chairperson is absent or temporarily unable to assume duties. In the event of
the death or resignation of the chairperson, the vice-chairperson will assume
the chairperson's office until a new chairperson can be elected as provided in
Section
9.16.060. The director will also serve as secretary of the commission.
(Reso. 1990-135 § 1, 1990; Ord. 1985-142 § 1 (part), 1985)
9.16.080   Method of commission operation.
   A.   Any five voting members of the commission constitutes a quorum. The
chairperson may delegate to the vice-chairperson or any members of the
commission the authority to call a meeting of the commission.
   B.   Regular commission meetings will be held at the call of the chairperson
or, in his absence, by the vice-chairperson.
   C.   The director of emergency services, with approval of the chairperson,
shall prepare an agenda before each meeting listing all known items of business
expected to be transacted. If possible, the agenda shall be prepared and mailed
to each member of the commission five days before the meeting date.
   D.   At the first regularly scheduled monthly meeting, or as soon thereafter
as possible, the commission shall adopt by-laws and regulations governing the
conduct of the commission's operations and business. Said by-laws and
regulations shall be effective as soon as approved by the Pima County board of
supervisors and the mayor and council of the city of Tucson.
   E.   Meetings of the commission shall be conducted pursuant to the Arizona
Open Meeting Law, A.R.S. § 38-431, et seq., and any applicable federal statutes
and regulations.
   F.   A special meeting of the commission may be called at any time by the
chairperson of the Pima County board of supervisors, the mayor of the city of
Tucson, or by the appropriate officials of any other future participating
political subdivision.
   G.   The chairperson shall conduct commission meetings according to Robert's
Rules of Order, except as modified by written by-laws of this Chapter.
(Reso. 1990-135 § 1, 1990; Ord. 1985-142 § 1 (part), 1985)
9.16.090   Definition, responsibilities and duties of the director of emergency
services.
   A.   The director is the chief executive for Tucson-Pima County department
of emergency services.
   B.   The director is responsible for emergency services administration for
Pima County and the city of Tucson. The director's responsibilities include,
but are not limited to, the following:
      1.   Development of plans for the survival of the maximum number of
people living in Tucson and Pima County in the event of natural or man-made
disaster;
      2.   Development of plans for the reconstruction of the community and its
institutions in the period following such disasters.
(Reso. 1990-135 § 1, 1990; Ord. 1985-142 § 1 (part), 1985)
9.16.100   Future participation in Tucson-Pima County emergency services plan.
   If, in the future, any other political subdivision within Pima County wishes
to enter the joint Tucson-Pima County emergency services effort, it may do so
by petition of its governing body to the Pima County board of supervisors and
to the mayor and council of the city of Tucson; the approval of both bodies
being necessary for acceptance. Upon such approval, the newly admitted
political subdivision shall share in the costs of the emergency services
program in terms of a per capita share based on its total population relative
to that of the city of Tucson. This sum will be prorated from the time of
acceptance until the end of the fiscal year.
(Reso. 1990-135 § 1, 1990; Ord. 1985-142 § 1 (part), 1985)
Chapter 9.20
CURFEW
Sections: 
9.20.010   Definitions.
9.20.020   Curfew for minors.
9.20.030   Parent, guardian or custodian.
9.20.010   Definitions.
   The following definitions shall apply throughout this chapter:
   A.   "Custodian" means any person, not a minor, who is in loco parentis to a
minor.
   B.   "Guardian" means any person, other than a parent, who has legal
guardianship of the person of a minor.
   C.   "Minor" means any person who has not yet reached eighteen years of age.
   D.   "Parent" means any natural or adoptive parent of a minor.
(Ord. 1996-65 § 1 (part), 1996: Ord. 1993-103 § 1 (part), 1993)
9.20.020   Curfew for minors.
   A.   It is unlawful for any minor, prior to his or her sixteenth birthday,
to be, remain, loiter or cruise in any vehicle in, about or upon any place in
the unincorporated area of the county away from his or her dwelling house or
usual place of abode between the hours of ten p.m. and five a.m. of the
following day.
   B.   It is unlawful for any minor, on or after his or her sixteenth
birthday, but prior to his or her eighteenth birthday, to be, remain, loiter or
cruise in any vehicle in, about or upon any place in the unincorporated area of
the county away from his or her dwelling house or usual place of abode between
the hours of twelve midnight and five a.m. of the following day.
   C.   The provisions of this section shall not apply to any minor when he or
she is accompanied by his or her parent, guardian, custodian or adult having
supervisorial custody, or when he or she is lawfully married, or when he or she
is on an emergency errand, or when he or she has been specifically directed to
the location on reasonable, legitimate business or some other activity by the
parent, guardian, custodian or adult having supervisorial custody.
   D.   Any minor violating this section is an incorrigible child.
(Ord. 1996-65 § 1 (part), 1996: Ord. 1993-103 § 1 (part), 1993)
9.20.030   Parent, guardian or custodian.
   A.   It is unlawful for the parent, guardian, custodian or adult having
supervisorial custody of any minor to permit the minor to be, remain, loiter or
cruise in any vehicle in, about or upon any place in the unincorporated area of
the county away from the dwelling house or usual place of abode of the minor in
violation of this chapter.
   B.   Any parent, guardian, custodian or adult having supervisorial custody
violating this section shall be guilty of a petty offense.
(Ord. 1996-65 § 1 (part), 1996: Ord. 1993-103 § 1 (part), 1993)
Chapter 9.25
REGULATION OF UNIDENTIFIED MASKED GROUPS CAUSING INTIMIDATION, EXEMPTING
IDENTIFIED LAW ENFORCEMENT OFFICERS
Sections:
9.25.010   Declaration of policy.
9.25.020   Regulation of unidentified masked groups.
9.25.030   Exemptions.
9.25.040   Violation—Penalty.
9.25.050   Scope.
9.25.010   Declaration of policy.
   The purpose of this chapter is to protect the inhabitants of Pima County
from intimidation caused by unidentified masked groups and prevent
unintentional interference with legitimate law enforcement operations within
the county.
(Ord. 2026-2 § 1, 2026)
9.25.020   Regulation of unidentified masked groups.
   Except as otherwise provided in this chapter, it is unlawful for any person
to gather in a group of two or more persons within the unincorporated county
upon publicly maintained streets and thoroughfares, public rights-of-way, or on
private lands without the consent of the lawful owner, when two or more persons
within the group:
   A.   Wear facial coverings obstructing more than 50% of the face; and
   B.   Carry on their person one or more of the following items:
      1.   Kinetic impact projectiles ("KIPs") including but not limited to
rubber bullets, plastic bullets, and beanbag rounds;
      2.   Flash-bang grenades;
      3.   Conducted energy devices ("CEDs", "TASERs", "stun guns");
      4.   Police-style batons;
      5.   Military or law-enforcement-style professional chemical agents
delivered via grenades, canisters, sprays, or aerosols designed to cause
causing intense burning, eye watering, and respiratory distress, including but
not limited to tear gas, pepper spray, Oleoresin Capsicum, 2-
Chlorobenzalmalononitrile, Chloroacetophenone, Dibenzoxazepine, Adamsite, and
Bromobenzylcyanide; and/or
      6.   Handcuffs, zip tie handcuffs, flex cuffs, or zip cuffs.
(Ord. 2026-2 § 1, 2026)
9.25.030   Exemptions.
   This chapter does not apply to any of the following:
   A.   A law enforcement or U.S. military officer of any local, state, or
federal agency or branch who has clearly visible on an outermost garment upon
the officer's person all of the following:
      1.   The name of the law enforcement agency or military branch employing
the officer; and
      2.   A unique identifier, such as an officer's badge number or legal
name.
   B.   A law enforcement or U.S. military officer of any local, state, or
federal agency or branch, who in the regular course of the officer's official
duties meets one or more of the following:
      1.   Does not carry distinguishing equipment and does not wear
distinguishing garments;
      2.   Is engaged in a clandestine undercover operation; or
      3.   Is part of a Specialized Elite Tactical Team and is engaged in a
response to an emergent or high-risk situation. "Specialized Elite Tactical
Team" as used in this chapter means a highly trained team of elite law
enforcement agents specially trained to respond to an unusually emergent, high-
risk, or dangerous situation, including Special Weapons and Tactics Teams
(SWAT), Counter Sniper Teams (CS), Special Response Teams (SRT), Counter
Assault Teams (CAT), and Special Operations Group (SOG). The status of
Specialized Elite Tactical Team must be a special or elite status and cannot
apply to the majority of officers in the agency or branch.
   C.   A person actively engaged in lawfully hunting wildlife. For the
purposes of this chapter, "actively engaged in lawfully hunting wildlife" does
not include traveling to or from a hunting location by way of a paved public
street or thoroughfare which is not approved as a lawful hunting location.
(Ord. 2026-2 § 1, 2026)
9.25.040   Violation—Penalty.
   A.   Each act of violation shall constitute a separate offense.
   B.   A person's first violation of this chapter constitutes a Class 3
misdemeanor and is subject to a fine of up to $500, up to 30 days in jail, and
up to one year of probation.
   C.   A person's second violation of this chapter constitutes a Class 2
misdemeanor and is subject to a fine of up to $750, up to four months in jail,
and up to two years of probation.
   D.   Any subsequent violation of this chapter constitutes a Class 1
misdemeanor and is subject to a $2,500 fine, up to six months in jail, and up
to three years of probation.
(Ord. 2026-2 § 1, 2026)
9.25.050   Scope.
   A.   Nothing in this chapter shall be construed as restricting or
interfering with any of the following:
      1.   The execution of court orders or lawful judicial warrants;
      2.   The rights of any person or entity under state or federal law;
      3.   Providing assistance to any local, state, or federal law enforcement
agency's investigative activities regarding suspected violations of criminal
law; or
      4.   The enforcement of criminal law.
   B.   To the fullest extent possible, this Chapter shall be construed in a
manner that is in accord with all of the following: the U.S. Constitution, the
Arizona Constitution, the Arizona Revised Statutes, the U.S. Code, and the Code
of Federal Regulations.
   C.   Any part of this chapter found invalid or unenforceable by a court of
law is severable; the remainder of the chapter remains in full force and
effect. The application of any part of this chapter found by a court of law to
be invalid or unenforceable as to any person or circumstances is severable; the
remainder of the chapter remains in full force and effect.
(Ord. 2026-2 § 1, 2026)
Chapter 9.30
REGULATION OF EXCESSIVE, UNNECESSARY AND ANNOYING NOISES
Sections: 
9.30.010   Applicability.
9.30.020   Purpose.
9.30.030   Definitions.
9.30.040   Impermissible sound levels.
9.30.050   Loud radios, sound sets, etc.
9.30.060   Vehicular noise.
9.30.070   Construction of buildings and other projects.
9.30.080   Exemptions.
9.30.090   Penalty.
9.30.100   Severability.
9.30.110   Effective date.
9.30.010   Applicability.
   This chapter shall not apply to any incorporated city, town or Indian
reservation. It shall apply only within the unincorporated areas of the county.
9.30.020   Purpose.
   It is hereby declared to be the policy of Pima County to prohibit excessive,
unnecessary and annoying noises from all sources. At and above certain level,
noises are detrimental to the health and welfare of the citizens of the county,
and it is in the best interest of the citizens of Pima County that such noises
be systematically eliminated.
(Ord. 1999-61 § 1 (part), 1999)
9.30.030   Definitions.
   The following definitions shall apply throughout this chapter unless a
different meaning is clearly indicated by the context:
   A.   Commercial property means any property occupied by business which sell,
rent, trade or store goods, or which provide a service.
   B.   Industrial property means any property occupied by land uses whose
primary operation involves manufacturing, assembling, processing or otherwise
treating raw materials, semi-finished products, or finished products for
packaging and distribution to either wholesale or retail markets.
   C.   Property line means the line which represents the legal limits of
property (including an apartment, condominium, room or other dwelling unit)
owned, leased or otherwise occupied by a person, business, corporation or
institution. In cases involving sound from an activity on a public street or
other public right-of-way, the property line shall be the nearest boundary of
the public right-of-way.
   D.   Residential property means any property, the dominant use of which is
nontransient occupancy of residential dwelling units.
   E.   Motor vehicle means any self-propelled vehicle operated within the
county, including but not limited to licensed or unlicensed vehicles,
automobiles, minibikes, go-carts, all terrain vehicles, and motorcycles.
   F.   Emergency work means any work performed to prevent or alleviate
physical trauma or property damage threatened or caused by an emergency which
has or may result in a disruption of service and which is necessary to protect
the health, safety and welfare of persons or property.
   G.   Emergency vehicle means vehicles of the fire, police and public service
departments and legally authorized ambulances and emergency vehicles of state
departments or any political subdivisions thereof and vehicles of public
service corporations.
   H.   Person means a human being and, as the context requires, an enterprise,
a public or private corporation, an unincorporated association, a partnership,
a firm, a society, a government, a governmental authority or an individual or
entity capable of holding a legal or beneficial interest in property.
(Ord. 2001-127 § 1 (part), 2001; Ord. 1999-61 § 1 (part), 1999)
9.30.040   Impermissible sound levels.
   In addition to the prohibited noises described in
9.30.050,
9.30.060 and
9.30.070, it shall be unlawful for any person to make or continue, or cause or
permit to be made or continued, any excessive, unnecessary or offensive noise
which disturbs the peace or quiet of any neighborhood or which causes
discomfort or annoyance to any reasonable person of normal sensitivity residing
in the area.
(Ord. 2001-127 § 1 (part), 2001; Ord. 1999-61 § 1 (part), 1999)
9.30.050   Loud radios, sound sets, etc.
   A.   It shall be unlawful for any person, including the owner or manager of
a restaurant, bar, inn, or resort of any kind, to operate or permit to be
operated any radio receiving set, phonograph, musical instrument, or sound
producing or sound reproducing mechanism, at any time in such a manner as to
permit the same to be hear at a distance of more than one hundred twenty-five
(125) feet from the property line or motor vehicle where such radio receiving
set, phonograph, or sound producing or sound reproducing mechanism is located,
when the sound of such radio receiving set, phonograph, musical instrument, or
sound producing or sound reproducing mechanism is operated in such a manner as
to create an excessive, unnecessary or offensive noise that a reasonable person
of normal sensitivity residing in the area is caused discomfort or annoyance.
   B.   It shall be unlawful for any person, including the owner or manager of
a restaurant, bar, inn, or resort of any kind, to operate or permit to be
operated any radio receiving set, phonograph, musical instrument, or sound
producing or sound reproducing mechanism, between the hours of 10:00 P.M. and
7:00 A.M. in such a manner that the sound from such radio set, phonograph,
musical instrument, sound producing or sound reproducing mechanism may be heard
beyond the property line from which it is operated or outside the motor vehicle
in which it is operated in such a manner as to create an excessive, unnecessary
or offensive noise that a reasonable person of normal sensitivity residing in
the area is caused discomfort or annoyance.
(Ord. 2001-127 § 1 (part), 2001; Ord. 1999-61 § 1 (part), 1999)
9.30.060   Vehicular noise.
   A.   It shall be unlawful for any person within any residential area of this
county to repair, rebuild or test any motor vehicle between the hours of 10:00
p.m. of one day and 7:00 a.m. of the next day in such a manner as to create an
excessive, unnecessary or offensive noise that a reasonable person of normal
sensitivity residing in the area is caused discomfort or annoyance.
   B.   No person shall operate or cause to operate any motor vehicle unless
the exhaust system of such vehicle:
      1.   Is free from defects which may cause sound level magnification,
      2.   Is equipped with a muffler,
      3.   Has not been modified in such a manner which will amplify or
increase the sound level emitted by the motor of such vehicle above that
emitted by a muffler originally installed on the vehicle as manufactured for
initial sale.
   C.   No person shall operate a motor vehicle in such a manner which creates
the squealing of tires in the roadway.
(Ord. 1999-61 § 1 (part), 1999)
9.30.070   Construction of buildings and other projects.
   A.   Noise limitations: Subject to the provisions of section
9.30.040, it shall be unlawful for any person to operate equipment or perform
any outside construction or repair work on buildings, structures or projects,
or to operate any pile driver, power shovel, pneumatic hammer, derrick, power
hoist or any other construction type device except within the time periods
specified below unless an appropriate permit has been obtained beforehand from
the county.
   B.   Construction start/stop times:
      1.   Concrete work: From April fifteenth to October fifteenth, inclusive,
concrete may be poured each day between the hours of 5:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m. or
at such other times as authorized by permit. From October sixteenth to April
Fourteenth, inclusive, concrete may be poured each day between the hours of 6:
00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. or at such times as authorized by permit.
      2.   Other type construction (residential zones): From April fifteenth to
October fifteenth, inclusive, all other construction or repair work shall not
begin prior to 6:00 a.m. and must stop by 7:00 p.m. each day in, or within five
hundred (500) feet of, a residential zone or at such other times as authorized
by permit. From October sixteenth to April fourteenth, inclusive, all other
construction or repair work shall not begin prior to 7:00 a.m. and must be
stopped by 7:00 p.m. each day in, or within five hundred (500) feet of, a
residential property or at such other times as authorized by permit.
      3.   Other type construction (commercial and industrial zones):
Construction and repair work in commercial and industrial zones, not within
five hundred (500) feet of a residential property, shall not begin prior to 5:
00 a.m. and must stop by 7:00 p.m. or at such other times as authorized by
permit.
      4.   Weekends and holidays excluded: Notwithstanding anything to the
contrary herein, construction or repair work shall not begin prior to 7:00 a.m.
and must stop by 7:00 p.m., and concrete pouring should not begin prior to 6:00
a.m. and must stop by 7:00 p.m. on any Saturday, Sunday or state or federal
holiday, unless such other times are authorized by permit.
   C.   Permits: Construction and repair work may be conducted at different
times and at higher noise levels than otherwise permitted, if upon written
application, a permit is obtained beforehand from the county administrator or
his designee. The permit shall be kept on the work site and shown to county
officials on request. In granting such permit, the county administrator or his
designee shall consider if construction noise in the vicinity of the proposed
work site would be less objectionable at night than during the daytime because
of different population levels or different neighboring activities; if
obstruction and interference with traffic, particularly on streets of major
importance, would be less objectionable at night than during the daytime; if
the kind of work to be performed emits noises at such a low level as to not
cause significant disturbance in the vicinity of the work site; if the
neighborhood of the proposed work site is of such a character wherein sleep
could be disturbed; if great economic hardship would occur if the work was
spread over a longer time; if the work will abate or prevent hazards to life or
property; if proposed early morning or night work is in the general public
interest; and, he shall prescribe such conditions, working times, types of
construction equipment to be used, and permissible noise emissions as he deems
to be required in the public interest. No permit shall be required to perform
emergency work as defined in section
9.30.030.
   D.   Revocation of permits: The county administrator or his designee may
revoke any permit granted hereunder upon complaint based upon substantial
evidence that the construction activity caused significant disturbance in the
vicinity of the work site.
(Ord. 1999-61 § 1 (part), 1999)
9.30.080   Exemptions.
   The following uses and activities shall be exempt from the provisions
contained in this article:
   A.   Heating and cooling equipment when it is functioning in accordance with
manufacturer's specifications and is in proper operating condition provided
that no unit may create an excessive, unnecessary or offensive noise causing
annoyance or discomfort to a reasonable person of normal sensitivity within any
sleeping or living area inside any dwelling unit;
   B.   Landscape maintenance equipment when it is functioning in accordance
with the manufacturer's specifications and with all mufflers and noise-reducing
equipment in use and in proper operating condition;
   C.   Nonamplified crowd noises resulting from activities such as those
planned by school, governmental or community groups, or organized sports except
for such noises generated at restaurants, bars, inns, or resorts of any kind;
   D.   Noises of safety signals, warning devices and emergency pressure relief
valves;
   E.   Noises resulting from any authorized emergency vehicle when responding
to an emergency call or acting in time of emergency;
   F.   Noises resulting from emergency work as defined in section
9.30.030;
   G.   Noises from the normal operation of railroad trains;
   H.   Noises from church chimes;
   I.   Power plant equipment during normal operation;
   J.   Noise created by any county vehicle, equipment or facility while being
operated for official use;
   K.   Operation of agricultural equipment in connection with farming
operations;
   L.   Any aircraft operated in conformity with, or pursuant to, federal law,
federal air regulations or air traffic control instructions issued pursuant to
or within duly adopted federal air regulations, together with any noise created
by aircraft operated under, or pursuant to, declaration of an emergency under
federal air regulations.
(Ord. 2001-127 § 1 (part), 2001; Ord. 1999-61 § 1 (part), 1999)
9.30.090   Penalty.
   A violation of any provision of this article shall be deemed and is declared
to be a public nuisance and any person who violates any of the provisions of
this article shall be guilty of a class 1 misdemeanor. Each day a violation
continues or exists shall be a separate offense subject to punishment as a
separate class 1 misdemeanor.
(Ord. 1999-61 § 1 (part), 1999)
9.30.100   Severability.
   If any provisions of this ordinance, or the application thereof to any
person or circumstance, is invalid, that invalidity shall not effect other
provisions or applications of this ordinance which can be given effect without
the invalid provisions or applications, and to this end the provisions of this
ordinance are severable.
(Ord. 1999-61 § 1 (part), 1999)
9.30.110   Effective date.
   This ordinance will be in full force and effective after thirty days from
the date of enactment.
(Ord. 1999-61 § 1 (part), 1999)
Chapter 9.40
FINGERPRINTING AND CRIMINAL HISTORY RECORDS CHECK OF PROSPECTIVE AND CURRENT
ATTENDANT CARE WORKERS
Sections: 
9.40.010   Authority to receive criminal history record information.
9.40.020   Fingerprinting of prospective and current attendant care workers.
9.40.030   Persons authorized to receive criminal history record information.
9.40.040   Annual sworn statement.
9.40.050   Persons prohibited from providing services.
9.40.010   Authority to receive criminal history record information.
   Pursuant to A.R.S. § 41-1750, pima health system is hereby authorized to
receive state and federal criminal history record information for the purpose
of evaluating the fitness of prospective and current attendant care workers.
(Ord. 2000-33 § 1, 2000)
9.40.020   Fingerprinting of prospective and current attendant care workers.
   As a condition of employment or continued employment with Pima County's pima
health system as an attendant care worker, in accordance with subparagraphs (1)
and (2) below, prospective and current attendant care workers shall submit a
full set of fingerprints on a standard fingerprint card to pima health system
for a state and federal criminal history records check pursuant to A.R.S. § 41-
1750 and Public Law 92-544. Pima health system shall forward those
fingerprints, accompanied by the appropriate fees, which shall be paid by pima
health system, to the Arizona department of public safety for the purpose of
obtaining a state and federal criminal history record check. The Department of
Public Safety is authorized to exchange this fingerprint data with the Federal
Bureau of Investigation.
      1.   As of the effective date of this chapter, each prospective attendant
care worker shall, within ten (10) business days of the successful completion
of the attendant care worker training program, furnish a full set of
fingerprints on a standard fingerprint card to the manager of human resources
for pima health system.
      2.   Within 45 days of the effective date of this chapter, each attendant
care worker currently employed by pima health system shall, as a condition of
continued employment, furnish a full set of fingerprints on a standard
fingerprint card to the manager of human resources for pima health system.
(Ord. 2000-33 § 1, 2000)
9.40.030   Persons authorized to receive criminal history record information.
   The manager of human resources for pima health system and the quality
management manager of pima health system are authorized to receive state and
federal criminal history record information for the purposes of evaluating the
fitness of prospective and current attendant care workers. Criminal history
record information received by either pima health system's manager of human
resources or quality management manager shall be used only for the purpose of
evaluating the fitness of prospective or current attendant care workers.
Secondary dissemination of such information is strictly prohibited. Pima health
system personnel shall comply with any relevant state and federal rules and
regulations regarding the dissemination of criminal history record information.
(Ord. 2000-33 § 1, 2000)
9.40.040   Annual sworn statement.
   A.   A prospective attendant care worker shall, with the full set of
fingerprints, complete and submit a notarized form, provided by pima health
system, indicating whether he has ever been convicted of, or is awaiting trial
on, any of the following criminal offenses in the state of Arizona or similar
offenses in any other state or jurisdiction:
      1.   Abuse of a vulnerable adult as defined in A.R.S. § 13-3623.
      2.   Sexual abuse.
      3.   Incest.
      4.   First or second degree murder.
      5.   Kidnapping.
      6.   Arson.
      7.   Sexual assault.
      8.   Sexual exploitation of a minor.
      9.   Contributing to the delinquency of a minor.
      10.   Commercial sexual exploitation of a minor.
      11.   Felony offenses involving distribution of marijuana or dangerous or
narcotic drugs.
      12.   Theft.
      13.   Robbery.
      14.   A dangerous crime against children as defined in A.R.S. § 13-
604.01.
      15.   Child abuse.
      16.   Sexual conduct with a minor.
      17.   Molestation of a child.
      18.   Manslaughter.
      19.   Aggravated assault.
      20.   Domestic violence.
      21.   Fraud or fraudulent schemes.
      22.   Assault within the last five years from the date of submitting a
full set of fingerprints to pima health system.
      23.   Possession or use of marijuana or a dangerous or narcotic drug
within the last five years from the date of submitting a full set of
fingerprints to Pima Health System.
   B.   A current attendant care worker shall, with the full set of
fingerprints submitted pursuant to Section
9.40.020(2), complete and submit a notarized form, provided by pima health
system, indicating whether he has ever been convicted of, or is awaiting trial
on, any of the criminal offenses enumerated in paragraph A of this section in
the state of Arizona or similar offenses in any other state or jurisdiction.
   C.   Each attendant care worker shall, as a condition of continued
employment, annually complete and submit a notarized form, provided by pima
health system, indicating whether, since the date of submitting his last sworn
statement, he has been convicted of, or is awaiting trial on, any of the
criminal offenses enumerated in paragraph A(1) through A(21) of this section,
or either of the following criminal offenses, in the state of Arizona or
similar offenses in any other state or jurisdiction:
      1.   Assault.
      2.   Possession or use of marijuana or a dangerous or narcotic drug.
(Ord. 2000-33 § 1, 2000)
9.40.050   Persons prohibited from providing services.
   Pima health system shall not allow any person to provide or continue to
provide services as an attendant care worker, if any of the following occur:
      1.   The criminal history records check or the sworn statement required
pursuant to Section
9.40.040 indicates that he is awaiting trial on, or has been convicted of, any
offense listed in Section
9.40.040(A); or,
      2.   The prospective or current attendant care worker fails or refuses to
submit fingerprints pursuant to Section
9.40.020; or
      3.   The prospective or current attendant care worker fails or refuses to
submit the sworn statement pursuant to Section
9.40.040; or,
      4.   The prospective or current attendant care worker submits a false
notarized statement regarding criminal offenses.
(Ord. 2000-33 § 1, 2000)

Chapter 9.70
UNDERAGE DRINKING
Section: 
9.70.010   Permitting or encouraging underage drinking.
9.70.010   Permitting or encouraging underage drinking.
   A.   No person eighteen years of age or older may knowingly permit or fail
to take reasonable action to prevent the illegal consumption of spirituous
liquor by an underage person on premises owned by the person or under the
person's control. This section does not apply to spirituous liquor used
exclusively as part of a religious service.
   B.   A person who violates this section is guilty of a Class 1 misdemeanor.
   C.   Spirituous liquor has the same meaning as in Title 4 of the Arizona
Revised Statutes.
(Ord. 2016-34, § 1, 2016: Ord. 2009-15 § 1, 2009)
Chapter 9.80
EXPLODING TARGETS
9.80.010   Short title.
9.80.020   Declaration of policy.
9.80.030   Definitions.
9.80.040   Mixed exploding targets prohibited; restrictions on sale.
9.80.050   Exceptions.
9.80.060   Violations; restitution required.
9.80.070   Seizure.
9.80.080   Violation—Penalty.
9.80.090   Severability.
9.80.010   Short title.
   This chapter may be cited and shall be known as the "Pima County Exploding
Target Ordinance."
(Ord. 2017-21 § 1 (part), 2017)
9.80.020   Declaration of policy.
   The purpose of this chapter is to protect the general public from the
hazardous use, sale, and unintended effects of mixed exploding targets. It is
further the policy of Pima County that any mixed exploding target be safely
used or destroyed in accordance with manufacturer recommendations.
(Ord. 2017-21 § 1 (part), 2017)
9.80.030   Definitions.
   A.   "Minor" means a person under the age of eighteen.
   B.   "Mixed exploding target" means a mixture or combination of chemicals
that can explode, detonate, or deflagrate upon impact by firearms ammunition
projectile. This includes commercial or homemade binary mixtures or synthesized
energetic material.
   C.   "Outdoor shooting range" means a permanently located and improved area
that is designed and operated for the use of rifles, shotguns, pistols,
silhouettes, skeet, trap, black powder, or any other similar sport shooting in
an outdoor environment.
   D.   "Person" means any individual, corporation, association, partnership,
firm, trustee, or legal representative.
(Ord. 2017-21 § 1 (part), 2017)
9.80.040   Mixed exploding targets prohibited; restrictions on sale.
   A.   Except as otherwise provided by this section, it is unlawful to sell,
offer, or expose for sale; use; explode; or possess any mixed exploding target.
   B.   It is unlawful for any person to sell any product marketed for use as a
mixed exploding target, or marketed for use as a component of a mixed exploding
target (1) to a minor or (2) to a person who reasonably appears to be a minor
without first requiring that person to display government-issued identification
proving that the person is not a minor.
(Ord. 2017-21 § 1 (part), 2017)
9.80.050   Exceptions.
   Section
9.80.040 does not apply to the use of mixed exploding targets:
   A.   On private land, provided that (1) any person using the mixed exploding
target obeys all applicable state laws regarding the discharge of firearms and
(2) there are no active fire restrictions in effect, as defined in A.R.S. § 37-
1303(B) or 36 C.F.R. § 261.50 on any land located in Pima County;
   B.   At a regulated outdoor shooting range as defined in Section
9.80.030, provided that the mixed exploding target is used immediately by the
person possessing it, and with the written permission of the owner, manager,
managing authority, or agency.
   C.   On any public land (1) that is not actively under a fire restriction as
defined in A.R.S. § 37-1303(B) or 36 C.F.R. § 261.50, and (2) on which the use
of mixed exploding targets is not prohibited by state or federal law, rule, or
policy.
(Ord. 2017-21 § 1 (part), 2017)
9.80.060   Violations; restitution required.
   A.   Upon a defendant's conviction for a violation of this chapter that
causes economic loss to any person, the court shall order that, in addition to
any monetary fine imposed, restitution to be paid by the defendant to any
person who suffered an economic loss caused by the defendant's conduct.
   B.   Restitution shall include any economic loss for which restitution may
be ordered for a misdemeanor offense under Arizona law.
(Ord. 2017-21 § 1 (part), 2017)
9.80.070   Seizure.
   The sheriff or other peace officer shall seize, remove, or cause to be
removed, at the expense of the owner, any product marketed for use as a mixed
exploding target, or marketed for use as a component of a mixed exploding
target that was offered or exposed for sale in violation of this chapter, or
any mixed exploding targets that were stored or possessed in violation of this
chapter.
(Ord. 2017-21 § 1 (part), 2017)
9.80.080   Violation—Penalty.
   A person violating a provision of this chapter is guilty of a class one
misdemeanor.
(Ord. 2017-21 § 1 (part), 2017)
9.80.090   Severability.
   If any provision of this chapter, or the application of any provision of
this chapter, is invalid, that invalidity shall not affect other provisions or
applications of this chapter. The provisions of this chapter are severable.
(Ord. 2017-21 § 1 (part), 2017)
Chapter 9.85
LOSS OR THEFT OF FIREARM—MANDATORY REPORTING
Sections:
9.85.010    Declaration of policy.
9.85.020    Definitions.
9.85.030    Mandatory reporting of loss or theft of firearm.
9.85.040    False reporting.
9.85.050    Exemptions.
9.85.060     Violation—Penalty.
9.85.010 Declaration of policy.
   The purpose of this chapter is to protect the inhabitants of Pima County by
aiding local law enforcement and the County Attorney in the enforcement of
A.R.S. § 13-3102(A)(5) and preventing the commission of crimes using firearms
obtained in violation of that statute. This chapter in no way affects the
possession, transfer, or storage of firearms because this chapter does not
provide means by which firearm possession could be revoked or transferred, nor
does it seek to regulate the storage of firearms.
(Ord. 2024-2 § 1 (part), 2024)
9.85.020 Definitions.
   A.   "Firearm" is defined as in A.R.S. § 13-3101.
   B.   "Person" is defined as in A.R.S. § 13-105.
(Ord. 2024-2 § 1 (part), 2024)
9.85.030 Mandatory reporting of loss or theft of firearm.
   A.   Except as otherwise provided in this chapter, it is unlawful for any
person to fail to report to a local law enforcement agency the knowing loss or
theft of a firearm.
   B.   The report of a loss or theft of a firearm pursuant to subsection A.
must be made in the jurisdiction in which the loss or theft occurred and within
forty-eight hours of the time the person knew or reasonably should have known
that the firearm had been lost or stolen.
   C.   Every person reporting a lost or stolen firearm pursuant to subsection
A. must report the make, model, and serial number of the firearm, if known by
the person, and any additional relevant information required by the local law
enforcement agency taking the report.
(Ord. 2024-2 § 1 (part), 2024)
9.85.040 False reporting.
   It is unlawful for any person to report to a local law enforcement agency
that a firearm has been lost or stolen, knowing the report to be false.
(Ord. 2024-2 § 1 (part), 2024)
9.85.050 Exemptions.
   This chapter does not apply to:
   A.   Any law enforcement agency or peace officer acting within the course
and scope of his or her employment or official duties if he or she reports the
loss or theft to his or her employing agency.
   B.   Any United States marshal or member of the Armed Forces of the United
States or the National Guard, while engaged in his or her official duties.
   C.   Any firearms dealer or manufacturer licensed under federal law and
subject to the reporting requirements of 18 U.S.C. 923(g)(6).
(Ord. 2024-2 § 1 (part), 2024)
9.85.060 Violation—Penalty.
   A person violating a provision of this chapter is guilty of a petty offense
and is subject to a penalty of up to one thousand dollars for each violation.
(Ord. 2024-2 § 1 (part), 2024)
Chapter 9.90
SEXUAL ORIENTATION CHANGE EFFORTS
9.90.010   Declaration of policy.
9.90.020   Definitions.
9.90.030   Prohibited conduct.
9.90.040   Violation; penalty.
9.90.050   Severability.
9.90.010   Declaration of policy.
   The purpose of this chapter is to protect the health, safety, and wellbeing
of minors in Pima County.
(Ord. 2017-22 § 1 (part), 2017)
9.90.020   Definitions.
   A.   "Minor" means a person under eighteen years of age.
   B.   "Person" means a natural person or, if the context permits it, any
corporation, association, partnership, firm, trustee, or other entity.
   C.   "Sexual orientation change efforts" means any practice in which a
person seeks to change another person's sexual orientation or gender identity.
"Sexual orientation change efforts" include efforts to change behaviors, sexual
or gender identities, or gender expressions, or to eliminate or reduce sexual
or romantic attractions or feelings toward persons of the same sex. "Sexual
orientation change efforts" do not include any communication that does not
itself seek to change the sexual orientation or gender identity of the person
who is the recipient of the communication.
(Ord. 2017-22 § 1 (part), 2017)
9.90.030   Prohibited conduct.
   No person may engage in sexual orientation change efforts with a minor in
exchange for a fee.
(Ord. 2017-22 § 1 (part), 2017)
9.90.040   Violation; penalty.
   A.   A violation of Section
9.90.030 is a civil infraction.
   B.   A person who violates Section
9.90.030 is subject to a civil penalty of up to two thousand five hundred
dollars for each violation.
(Ord. 2017-22 § 1 (part), 2017)
9.90.050   Severability.
   If any provision of this chapter, or the application of any provision of
this chapter, is invalid, that invalidity shall not affect other provisions or
applications of this chapter. The provisions of this chapter are severable.
(Ord. 2017-22 § 1 (part), 2017)
